summary.text: Chronological dating is the work of giving an object or event a date in the past so it can be placed in an established chronology.
Methods are classed as relative, which place things before or after other events, or absolute, which give a specific date or date range.
Absolute dating relies mainly on radiometric methods, such as radiocarbon dating, which reliably reaches back about 50,000 years.

facts.label: Radiocarbon reach
facts.value: Reliable up to about 50,000 years ago

facts.label: Dating fired bricks
facts.value: Thermoluminescence shows roughly when they were fired

facts.label: Fields that use it
facts.value: History, geology, archaeology, astronomy, forensic science

items.prompt: A playwright's main source for a play was a book that first came out in 1587. What can historians safely say about when the play was written?

options.label: It was written some time after 1587
It was written exactly in 1587
It was written some time before 1587
Nothing, without a date written on it

items.explain: A work cannot use a source that did not yet exist, so 1587 is the post quem date: the play was written after it, as with Shakespeare's Henry V.

items.prompt: A researcher can show that one layer of a dig is older than the layer above it, but cannot give either layer a year. What kind of dating is this?

options.label: Absolute dating
Radiometric dating
Relative dating
Thermoluminescence dating

items.explain: Relative dating places things on a timeline relative to other events or artifacts without fixing an absolute age.

items.prompt: Historians want to know roughly how many years ago the bricks of an old church were fired in a kiln. Which technique suits this?

options.label: Radiocarbon dating
Uranium–uranium dating
Cementochronology
Thermoluminescence dating

items.explain: Thermoluminescence dating of bricks shows approximately how many years ago the material was fired; it was used this way on St. James Church in Toruń.

items.prompt: A rock layer is hard to date directly, but it holds fossil pollen. Why can the pollen help place the layer in time?

options.label: Pollen grains keep a record of the year they were shed
Some plant species are known to belong to a set point in time
Pollen decays at a fixed rate like a radioactive clock
Pollen only survives in layers younger than a century

items.explain: Some plant species, extinct or not, are well known to belong to a particular position in the time scale, so their pollen acts as a relative marker.

items.prompt: A team finds charcoal from a hearth they believe is around half a million years old. Why is radiocarbon dating a poor fit?

options.label: Charcoal holds no organic material at all
The method only works on human bones
It is far beyond the method's reliable range
Fire resets every dating clock to zero

items.explain: Radiocarbon dating reliably measures dates only up to approximately 50,000 years ago.

items.prompt: An excavator finds a coin in a layer of a site. Why can a coin be such a handy dating clue?

options.label: Many coins carry the year they were made
Metal coins never move between layers
Coins glow when heated, showing their age
Coins are only found in the oldest layers

items.explain: Many coins have their date of production written on them, or their period of use is known from the historical record.
